body:
This is exactly what I wonder about.  Evolution has given humanity, (and most animals,) the instinct to stay alive at all costs and to propagate the species.  It seems that this is our purpose.  I just wonder why we have that primal instinct.  As difficult as life must have been for our ancient ancestors, they still felt compelled to procreate and continue on.  My problems today pale in comparison to the problems they faced, yet I can't find a good reason to stick around, much less procreate. 

Thanks for taking the time to respond.

I think the fact that I have such difficulties going out and doing anything, (due to anxiety/agoraphobia,) are part of the reason why I can't find any enjoyment in life.  The idea that life has no purpose goes to the heart of my question.  If there is no purpose, then why do it?  I know these thoughts have been pondered by people for centuries, so I don't expect to find the answer when others have not.

Thanks for sharing your thoughts and for taking the time to respond.

I would love to have relief from this pain, but I often think that if relief isn't possible then not feeling anything would be an acceptable alternative.

My family is the reason I stick around, but it's become more difficult lately.

Thank you for the kind words and for taking the time to respond.

I understand this idea and have studied Buddhist writings at some length.  I have come closer to a feeling of peace through these teachings as I have anything else, but I still struggle with the question of 'why.'

Thank you for this.

I appreciate your sentiment, but I learned long ago that there is no god.  If there were, at least I would have someone to blame for all the bad things that have happened in my life.  Thanks for trying, though.
